info.description:
## Overview

Use the MailGraf REST API to connect a CRM, commerce platform, form, workflow
or your own service to a MailGraf account. The current v1 API lets you:

- create and update contacts, and unsubscribe them
- read each contact's engagement (temperature, stars, last open or click),
  tags and lists, and fetch only the contacts that changed since your last sync
- request a double opt-in confirmation instead of adding a contact directly
- discover lists and manage list membership
- discover tags, and add or remove them on contacts
- discover the account's custom fields
- add email addresses to the account block list
- send custom behaviour events that can start automations
- read campaigns and their delivery reports
- subscribe an endpoint to webhook events

The production base URL is `https://api.mailgraf.com/v1`. This reference
is the canonical contract for the public API. It does not include the
session-based endpoints used internally by the MailGraf web application.

## Quick start

Create a key in **Settings > Developers > API keys**, copy it when it is shown, then
check the account connected to the key:

    curl https://api.mailgraf.com/v1/account \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer mg_live_..."

If the request succeeds, you can upsert a contact with `POST /v1/contacts`.
MailGraf uses the email address as the identity for a contact upsert.

## Authentication

Send your API key as a Bearer token on every request:

    Authorization: Bearer mg_live_...

Keys are created in **Settings > Developers > API keys** and shown only once. A
revoked key stops working immediately.

## Connected apps (OAuth)

An app such as an MCP client or Zapier can connect to an account without copying
a key: the user approves it on a MailGraf permission screen and the app receives
an access token. Tokens use the same `Authorization: Bearer` header and pass the
same account, plan and rate-limit checks as API keys. Two extra rules apply: the
permissions the user approved, and the resource the token was issued for.

Permissions (scopes):

- `read`: every GET endpoint
- `write`: the endpoints that create or change data
- `test_send`: sending a test email through the MCP server
- `send`: sending or scheduling a campaign and starting an automation through
  the MCP server, each only after the user confirms a review summary; it also
  covers test emails

Ask for permissions with the space-separated `scope` parameter of the
authorization request. If an app asks for none, an app that registered itself
or uses a metadata URL (see below) receives `read write send` and any other app
receives `read`. The permission screen shows
what the app will receive, and the user approves or cancels. A request outside
the approved permissions returns **403**.

Resource: a token works on one resource only, either this API or the MCP
server. Send `resource=https://api.mailgraf.com/v1` for this API or
`resource=https://api.mailgraf.com/mcp` for the MCP server with the
authorization request. If you send `resource` again with the token request, it
must match. Without it, apps that register themselves or identify with a
metadata URL receive an MCP token; other apps receive a token for this API. A
token used on the other resource returns **403**.

Discovery: `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` for the authorization
server, `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1` and
`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` for the two resources. Flow:
authorization code with PKCE (S256) at `/oauth/authorize`, `POST /oauth/token`
for the exchange and for refresh (refresh tokens rotate), `POST /oauth/revoke`
to end a connection.

An app identifies itself in one of two ways:

- Self-registration at `POST /oauth/register` (public clients using PKCE).
- A client ID metadata document: the app uses an `https` URL as its
  `client_id`, which is how Claude connects by default. MailGraf fetches the
  JSON document at that URL (HTTPS, public address, no redirects, up to 64 KB),
  checks its `redirect_uris` and keeps it for 24 hours. A `scope` value in the
  document limits the permissions the app can ask for.

Users see and disconnect connected apps in **Settings > Developers > MCP**.


## MCP server

AI assistants that support the Model Context Protocol (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini,
Cursor and others) can work with your account through the MailGraf MCP server:

    https://api.mailgraf.com/mcp

Add it in your AI tool as a remote MCP server (some tools call this a custom
connector), then approve the connection on the MailGraf permission screen. The
address is also shown in **Settings > Developers > MCP**. Tools without
OAuth support can send an API key as the Bearer token instead. An API key gives
the assistant every permission, including send; connect with OAuth when you want
to limit what it can do.

With the read permission the assistant can look at campaigns, their reports,
content (subject, preview text, body and links) and link clicks, and compare
campaigns. It can read an account overview, deliverability by mailbox provider,
audience gains and losses and unsubscribe reasons; check send readiness,
send-time optimisation and sending domains; list automations with their
performance, saved templates and brand settings; see lists, segments, segment
presets, tags and custom fields; look up one contact by email; preview a segment
or how many contacts a bulk action would touch; and read verification and bounce
test results. With the write permission it can also add or update contacts (up to
1,000 per call, stating the consent source), manage list membership, unsubscribe
or block an address, create custom fields, segments and lists, prepare campaigns
(draft, content from a saved template or HTML, audience and recipient count,
pre-send review) and run bulk actions on the MailGraf server: add or remove a
tag, add to or remove from a list, set a field value, or block, for a whole
list, segment, tag or all contacts; set up automations from templates, update
brand settings, fix text and links in a draft and start verifications (a free
bounce test, or a full verification after you confirm the credits). Only counts
come back to the chat. With the send permission (or `test_send` for test emails
only) it can send a test email and, after you confirm the review summary, send
or schedule a campaign or activate an automation, and pause, resume, cancel or
stop one.

Contact lists are never returned in bulk and there is no export through MCP.
Deleting contacts, bulk delete and removing block-list entries are not
available, and nothing is sent without a confirmed review. Every call passes the same gates as this
API (account isolation, the plan's API access, the rate limit) and appears in the
API request monitor with the tool name.

The server also offers eleven ready-made prompts that supporting assistants show
in their command menu: a weekly summary, a campaign review, subject line ideas,
comparing recent campaigns, a deliverability check, audience health, cleaning
inactive contacts, the best time to send, preparing a campaign, setting up an
automation and a pre-send list check.

## Pagination

List endpoints return `items` together with `next_cursor` and `has_more`.
Pass `cursor=<next_cursor>` to fetch the next page; `limit` accepts 1-100
(default 50). Ordering is newest first.

## Keeping a CRM in step

Every contact carries its engagement: `temperature` (new, hot, cooling or
cold), `engagement_stars` (0 to 5 in half steps), `last_engaged_at` (the last
real open or click), `first_opened_at` and `engagement_updated_at`, together
with its `tags` and `lists`.

To copy changes to a CRM such as Pipedrive or HubSpot, store the time you
start each sync and call `GET /v1/contacts?updated_since=<that time minus one
hour>` next time, following `next_cursor` to the last page. The hour of
overlap covers opens and clicks that reach MailGraf a little after they
happen; writing the same values twice is harmless. A contact is returned when its
profile or status changed, it opened or clicked an email, or its temperature
or star rating changed. Tag and list changes do not count; use the
`contact.tag_added`, `contact.tag_removed`, `contact.list_added` and
`contact.list_removed` webhooks for those. MailGraf scores contacts once a
day, so a daily sync is enough. Match the contact in your CRM by email.

## Rate limits

Each key may make **120 requests per 60 seconds**. Above the
limit the API responds with **429** and a `Retry-After` header containing the
number of seconds to wait. Repeated failed authentication from one IP is
locked out temporarily.

## Errors

Errors use a `detail` field. Most errors return a readable string. A 422
request-validation response may instead contain a list of field-level issues.
The reference for each operation lists the status codes it can return:

- **401**: the API key is missing, invalid or revoked
- **403**: the account's plan does not include API access, or an OAuth token
  lacks the permission or was issued for the other resource
- **404**: the requested account resource was not found
- **422**: the request could not be validated or processed
- **429**: the API key has exceeded its rate limit
- **503**: rate-limit protection is temporarily unavailable

## Idempotency

`POST /v1/events` accepts an optional `event_id`; sending the same id twice
stores the event once and returns `created: false`.

## Webhooks

Outbound webhooks are configured in **Settings > Developers > Webhooks** or
created with `POST /v1/webhooks`, which is how an integration such as Zapier
subscribes to events. An account can hold up to 10 webhooks.

Events: `contact.subscribed`, `contact.unsubscribed`, `contact.complained`,
`email.delivered`, `email.bounced`, `campaign.sent`, `form.submitted`,
`contact.list_added`, `contact.list_removed`, `contact.tag_added` and
`contact.tag_removed`.

Every delivery is a JSON `POST` with the same shape:

    {
      "type": "email.bounced",
      "event_id": 81234,
      "occurred_at": "2026-09-26T10:15:00+00:00",
      "contact": {"id": 5012, "email": "ada@example.com"},
      "campaign": {"id": 311, "name": "September newsletter"},
      "data": {"sub_type": "hard"}
    }

Fields without a value are `null`. `campaign` is set when the event belongs to
a campaign.
`data` depends on the event: list and tag events carry `list` or `tag` (`id`,
`name`) and `source` (`panel`, `automation`, `form`, `api` or `mcp`);
`form.submitted` carries `form`, `mode` and the submitted
`values`, with `contact.id` still `null` because the contact is created later;
`campaign.sent` carries the send counts (`sent`, `failed`, `not_sent`,
`accept_unknown`); email events may carry `sub_type`. `event_id` identifies a
stored contact event and is `null` for the others.

Delivery rules:

- A delivery succeeds when your endpoint answers with a 2xx status within
  7 seconds. Redirects and every other answer count as failures.
- A failed delivery is retried after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes and
  2 hours, five attempts in total.
- If ten deliveries in a row fail all their attempts, MailGraf turns the
  webhook off and notifies the account. Turn it back on in the webhook settings.
- Deliveries can arrive more than once and out of order. Answer quickly and
  process the payload afterwards; when `event_id` is set, use it to skip
  repeats.

Every delivery carries an `X-MailGraf-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>` header. It
is an HMAC-SHA256 of `"{t}.{body}"` computed with your endpoint's signing
secret. Always verify the signature against the RAW request body before
trusting a payload, for example in Python:

    import hashlib, hmac

    def verify(secret: str, header: str, raw_body: bytes) -> bool:
        parts = dict(item.split("=", 1) for item in header.split(","))
        signed = parts["t"].encode() + b"." + raw_body
        expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), signed, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
        return hmac.compare_digest(expected, parts["v1"])

The Webhooks settings page in MailGraf shows the same check in Python and Node.js.

get.description:
Use this endpoint to confirm which MailGraf account the API key belongs to.

It is a lightweight connection check after creating or rotating a key.
The response does not expose billing, users or other account settings.

200.description: The MailGraf account connected to the API key.

401.description: The API key is missing, invalid or revoked.

Use this endpoint to retrieve contacts, ordered newest first.

Pass the previous response's `next_cursor` to continue through a large
account without offset drift. Use `email` when you need an exact,

post.description:
Use this endpoint to record a custom behaviour event for an existing contact.

The contact must already exist; upsert it first (404 otherwise). Events
can start automations through the "Contact sends a custom event" trigger.
Optional `event_id` makes the call idempotent; `occurred_at` accepts
ISO 8601 within the last 24 hours. Properties are limited to 8 KB; any
`email` property is stripped before storage.

Three order events keep one order record per `order_id` (falling back to
`order_number`, then `event_id`): `order_placed` (also `order_created`) with
`total`, `currency`, `order_date` and `items`; `order_paid` with the amount
collected in `total` (defaults to the order total); `order_refunded` with the
refunded `amount` (or the cumulative `refunded_total`; without either, the whole
payment). A late refund updates the same order, so campaign revenue reports stay
net. Each event refreshes the contact's order fields: `last_order_at`,
`last_order_total`, `last_order_currency`, `order_count`, and `total_spent` with
`total_spent_currency` (payments minus refunds, in the currency of the first
order; an unpaid order is counted but adds nothing, and an order in another
currency is counted but not added). The fields are created on first use. Totals
you imported into `order_count` and `total_spent` are kept: the first order event
moves them to `imported_order_count` and `imported_total_spent`, and new orders
add on top. An order is attributed to the email the contact clicked in the last
5 days, or opened in the last 2 days, before the order; this can be a campaign or
an automation email.

Send products in `items` on `order_placed` and `order_paid`; they are stored with
the order and replaced each time the list arrives. Each item takes `product_id`
(or the older `id`), `variant_id`, `sku`, `name`, `variant_name`, `price`,
`quantity`, `image_url` and `url`, for example `[{"product_id": 7, "variant_id": 71,
"name": "Coffee", "variant_name": "250 g", "price": 74.95, "quantity": 2}]`. An item
needs a `product_id` or a `name`; up to 100 items are kept per order. Tools that
cannot nest data can send the same list as a top-level `items` field instead.

An automation that starts with a custom event keeps that event's properties, so its
emails can use them: plain values as merge tags (`{{event.cart_url}}`,
`{{event.total}}`) and `items` in the cart items block. For a cart reminder, send
`cart_updated` as soon as the cart changes, with `cart_url`, `total`, `currency` and
`items` such as `[{"name": "Coffee", "price": 74.95, "quantity": 2, "image_url":
"https://...", "url": "https://..."}]`; the automation waits, shows the latest cart
and stops when an exit event such as `order_placed` arrives.

200.description: The idempotency result and event id.
